proposals.after: His father was Yang, courtesy name Faxiu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 法脩 is Faxiu; Faxing misreads 脩 as 興.

proposals.before: His father was Yang, styled Faxing.
proposals.after: His father was Yang, styled Faxiu.

proposals.before: Early in the reign of Emperor Gaozu, he entered the kingdom with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others. He was made General of Illustrious Might and Marquis of Hejian; Chengxin was made General of Bright Prestige. Both were received as honored guests and given slaves, horses, cattle, and silks.
proposals.after: Early in the reign of Emperor Gaozu, he entered the kingdom with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townsmen Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others. He was made General of Illustrious Might and Viscount of Hejian; Chengxin was made General of Bright Prestige. Both were received as honored guests and given slaves, horses, cattle, and silks.
proposals.reason: 河間子 is Viscount of Hejian; 子 is not Marquis (侯).

proposals.before: Early in the Yan Chang era he was made Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: Early in the Yanchang era he was made Minister over the Masses.
proposals.reason: 延昌 is Yanchang; 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: At the beginning of Yan Chang, he was transferred to Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Yanchang, he was transferred to Minister over the Masses.
proposals.reason: 延昌 is Yanchang; 司徒 is not Grand Tutor.

proposals.before: In the second year of Yongxi Emperor Chu posthumously granted him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Jizhou.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Chu posthumously granted him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: Missing comma between era name Yongxi and Emperor Chu makes the English ungrammatical.

proposals.before: As the son of a meritorious minister and for his own achievements, he became garrison commander of Woye, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuchang, and was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
proposals.after: As the son of a meritorious minister and for his own achievements, he became garrison commander of Woye, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuchang, and was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
proposals.reason: 富昌子 is Viscount of Fuchang; 子 is not Marquis.

proposals.before: He was made Grand Tutor while retaining his post as Palace Attendant. The appointment was conferred at his home.
proposals.after: He was made Minister over the Masses while retaining his post as Palace Attendant. The appointment was conferred at his home.
proposals.reason: 司徒公 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).

proposals.before: An envoy with imperial authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral.
proposals.after: An envoy with imperial authority went to the Duke of Anding's residence to supervise the funeral.
proposals.reason: Collation note indicates 安定下脫公第; Guozhen died/buried at Luoyang, not Anding the place.

proposals.before: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan County.
proposals.after: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingyuan County.
proposals.reason: Collation note: original enfeoffment was 清淵; 清泉 is Tang taboo avoidance in Beishi-derived text.

decisions.reason: The courtesy name 法脩 is Faxiu. Faxing would require a different final character.
The literal field must use the same correct reading, Faxiu, for 法脩.
子 is the fourth of the five noble ranks and is conventionally translated Viscount, whereas Marquis would represent 侯.
延昌 is the Yanchang era name, and 司徒 is Minister over the Masses rather than Grand Tutor (太傅).
The literal field contains the same era-name spacing and office mistranslation and should match the source terminology.

decisions.after: In the second year of Yongxi, the Deposed Emperor posthumously granted him the titles Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Within and Without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Jizhou.
decisions.reason: The comma is required, but 出帝 is the regnal designation 'the Deposed Emperor,' not a personal name 'Emperor Chu.'
富昌子 is the title Viscount of Fuchang; Marquis would correspond to 富昌侯.
司徒公 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅).
The chapter's collation note explains that 公第 has dropped out after 安定. Hu Guozhen died and was buried at Luoyang, so the envoy went to the Duke of Anding's residence, not to Anding.
The collation note identifies 清泉 as Tang taboo substitution and restores the historical fief name 清淵, Qingyuan.
